summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, a history of avascular necrosis of the right hip, and prior osteosarcoma was admitted for a sickle cell pain crisis characterized by severe right hip and leg pain unresponsive to home hydromorphone. She had recently recovered from a mild viral illness. Imaging revealed chronic bilateral avascular necrosis with a small area of active infarction in the right femoral head, but no collapse. She was treated with IV fluids, IV Dilaudid transitioned to oral analgesics, and supportive care. Her pain improved, and she was discharged home with stable vital signs, a prescription for a lidocaine patch, and follow-up plans with hematology, orthopedics, and her primary care provider. A chest X-ray showed no acute chest syndrome, and labs indicated stable hemoglobin and resolved somnolence. Mildly prominent inguinal lymph nodes were noted incidentally, prompting recommendation for future monitoring given her cancer history.
problems: Personal history of malignant neoplasm of bone
